summary: Describes a URN namespace for the National Computerization Agency (NCA) for naming persistent digital resources such as music, videos, texts, images and e-books. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: A library gives each book a permanent code. This memo gives digital items like songs and videos from one agency a permanent name that does not change.

subtitle: A permanent naming system for Korea's digital content managed by the National Computerization Agency.

tldr.problem: Korea's National Computerization Agency manages millions of digital resources (music, videos, texts, e-books, research reports) but lacks a standardized way to assign globally unique, persistent names to them.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC establishes a URN namespace for Universal Content Identifiers (UCI), where each digital resource receives a unique identifier composed of a registration agency code and a content code, with optional qualifiers for versions or editions.
tldr.outcome: Digital content in Korea can now be identified and resolved persistently via URN infrastructure, enabling interoperability in the digital content supply chain.

today: RFC 4179 is an Informational document that formally registers the UCI namespace with IANA. The UCI system is in active operation in Korea under NCA's administration, providing persistent identifiers for Korean digital content. The resolution servers and registration agency infrastructure enable organizations to register, identify, and resolve digital resources using the URN namespace.

sections.title: Why Korea Needs Permanent Digital Identifiers
sections.content:
The National Computerization Agency (NCA) is a Korean government-sponsored organization that supervises digitalization projects involving millions of technical papers, cultural properties, educational materials, and research reports. These digital resources are produced, managed, and preserved by various organizations according to standards set by NCA.

When many organizations collaborate to manage digital content, they need a way to refer to items that is independent of storage location, format, or which organization currently holds the content. A permanent identifier serves this purpose: it stays the same even if a file moves to a different server or the organization managing it changes.

NCA wanted to issue globally unique, persistent identifiers under a URN (Uniform Resource Name) scheme, where each resource is assigned an identifier that can be looked up to find the current location and metadata. The UCI (Universal Content Identifier) scheme, already in development and use within Korea's content systems, was the natural choice for formalization as a URN namespace.
sections.plainLanguage: Many organizations in Korea digitize and share music, books, research papers, and videos. They needed a system to give each item a permanent name that works no matter which organization stores it or what format it is in.

sections.title: How UCI Identifiers Are Structured
sections.content:
A UCI identifier consists of a prefix code and a content code. The prefix code is assigned to a registration agency or subordinate registrant and identifies which organization or category manages that set of resources. Prefix codes have a format like G3000+music (for music administered by a particular agency) or I600 (for another registration agency).

The content code contains an instance code (a unique code for each individual digital resource, such as cii90007 or 8987409) and an optional qualifier (used to distinguish versions or editions, designated by letters C, R, or F). For example, urn:uci:I700-2987098 identifies a resource registered by registration agency I700 with instance code 2987098.

The full syntax conforms to RFC 2141 (URN Syntax). The prefix is case-insensitive for matching, but the remainder of the identifier is case-sensitive. Characters allowed include alphanumeric characters, hyphens, colons, and plus signs in the prefix, and in the content code, alphanumeric characters, percent-encoded sequences, and special characters from the set ()+-,.=@;$_!*'.
sections.plainLanguage: A UCI name has two parts: a code for which organization manages it (like a library branch), and a unique code for the item itself (like a book number). Some items also have extra codes for different versions or editions.

sections.title: How UCI Identifiers Are Resolved
sections.content:
Resolution is a two-step process. Global resolution is performed by NCA's central resolver, which parses the registration agency code from the UCI identifier and directs the query to the appropriate registration agency. Local resolution is then performed by that registration agency, which parses and resolves the remainder of the identifier to return metadata and locator information about the digital resource.

NCA operates a public global resolution server at http://rootadmin.uci.or.kr:9000/ followed by the UCI identifier. Validation of prefix codes is available both online and offline, and the validity of the full identifier can be checked via the online resolution service.
sections.plainLanguage: To find a resource, you ask the national office (NCA) which organization manages that prefix code, then ask that organization for the specific item. Both lookups are available online.

sections.title: Ensuring Uniqueness and Persistence
sections.content:
Each registration agency maintains a list of subordinate registrants and the identifiers assigned to that agency. NCA ensures uniqueness by using software tools to check that a UCI identifier is not being reassigned and is assigned to at most one resource during the registration process.

As a government-sponsored entity, NCA provides long-term persistence guarantees. NCA operates backup services and makes efforts to find a substitute operator if a registration agency goes out of operation, ensuring that the UCI namespace remains functional and that assigned identifiers do not become orphaned. This commitment to persistence is critical for digital preservation, as referenced resources must remain accessible over decades.
sections.plainLanguage: Rules make sure each resource gets exactly one permanent name and never gets reassigned. If an organization that manages some names shuts down, NCA helps find someone else to keep those names working.
